about: Consensus vectors of the canonical template with strict frames, written once and never regenerated: on any later commit a mismatch is a finding to explain, not a reason to update this file. The byte-level sections, eip712 through evm_advance, are carried unchanged from consensus_vectors_v1.json, which pinned them on Rust 1.95.0 / alloy-core 1.6.1. The guest section was computed once from the reference scheduler and the wallet, and the scheduler_only section from the reference scheduler alone. Bytes are 0x-prefixed hex; uint256 values are 0x-prefixed hex quantities.

guest.about: Scenarios replayed from genesis on the devnet template, whose scheduler configuration is config. Each step is the next InputBox input: its sender (a name in senders), block, timestamp and payload (a name in payloads). Then what the scheduler made of it: outcome, and for a rejected batch reject, whose reason is a diagnostic. Then txs, the transactions it handed out in order: a direct by its input index, a user op whole, each with the batch nonce it was handed out under, and for a user op whether the executor ran it or skipped it for its nonce. Then outputs, by name in outputs, and scheduler, the machine's scheduler report after the input. A scenario ends with the machine's state report, or its keccak256 when it is long.

scenarios.name: safe_block_at_inclusion_block
scenarios.about: A frame at its batch's own inclusion block is rejected; the same batch one block later drains.

scenarios.name: first_frame_below_clock
scenarios.about: After a frame raises the clock, a batch whose first frame lies below it is rejected and one at it is accepted.

scenarios.name: stale_batch
scenarios.about: The backstop drains a deposit before a stale batch is skipped; a batch exactly one block inside the window is accepted at the kept nonce.

scenarios.name: wrong_batch_nonce
scenarios.about: A batch at the wrong nonce changes nothing; the right one drains and runs its op; the next skips the spent op nonce.

scenarios.name: fee_price_out_of_range
scenarios.about: A tail frame priced above the maximum exponent rejects the whole batch before its first frame drains; a frame at the maximum is accepted.

scenarios.name: backstop_drains_queued_directs
scenarios.about: Directs queued for the whole window execute when a later input arrives, even an undecodable batch or another direct.

scenarios.name: direct_over_payload_cap
scenarios.about: A direct one byte over the payload cap never joins the fridge but takes its input index; one at the cap joins and executes.

scenarios.name: fee_cap_below_price
scenarios.about: An op whose max fee is below its frame's price is never handed out and leaves its nonce unspent; the same nonce at a covering cap executes.

scenarios.name: wrong_nonce_op
scenarios.about: Ops at a nonce other than the sender's next are handed out and skipped; the one at the next nonce executes.

scenarios.name: underfunded_op
scenarios.about: An op whose sender cannot pay the price is charged what the sender has and executes; the next op pays nothing and its transfer fails.

scenarios.name: directs_queue_then_drain_with_ops
scenarios.about: Directs stay queued across several inputs, then each frame drains those at or below its safe block before its ops; a later direct waits above the clock.

scenarios.name: rejected_batch_after_drain
scenarios.about: Right after a frame drains, a replayed batch and a batch with decreasing safe blocks are rejected and drain nothing; the next valid batch drains the rest.

scenarios.name: empty_batch_at_any_age
scenarios.about: An empty batch is accepted at any age and spends its nonce; the backstop runs before it.

scenarios.name: later_frame_at_inclusion_block
scenarios.about: A batch whose first frame lies below its inclusion block but whose last frame sits at it is rejected; the same batch one block later drains both directs.

scenarios.name: backstop_runs_before_a_dropped_direct
scenarios.about: The backstop runs before a direct the cap drops: the overdue direct executes though the arriving one never joins, and a later batch drains the rest.

scheduler_only.about: Scenarios for the scheduler alone, under config, whose fridge bound of 2 lets a few inputs overflow it; the wallet's bound of 16384 keeps overflow out of the guest scenarios. Senders, payloads, chain_id and app_contract are the guest section's. A step is as in a guest scenario without fates, outputs or l2_tx_count, and scheduler is the scheduler's state after the input. A resume case gives an exported state and the re-supplied range, each input with its InputBox index; result is resumed or refused, refusal names the reference's reason as a diagnostic, and then continues a resumed scheduler from the state's l1_input_count.

scenarios.name: overflow_drains_the_oldest_whole_block
scenarios.about: A direct arriving at a full fridge drains every direct of the oldest block, more than it needs, and raises the clock; a frame at the raised clock is accepted.

scenarios.name: overflow_never_drains_the_arriving_block
scenarios.about: A direct at the block of every queued direct joins a full fridge, so the bound is soft by one block; the next block's direct drains them all.

scenarios.name: overflow_raises_the_clock_past_a_frame
scenarios.about: The clock an overflow drain raises rejects a batch whose first frame lies below it; a frame at it is accepted and drains nothing newer.

scenarios.name: dropped_direct_never_overflows
scenarios.about: A direct over the payload cap arriving at a full fridge drains nothing; the next admitted direct does.

resume.name: resume_rebuilds_the_fridge
resume.about: The range's admitted directs refill the fridge, skipping a dropped direct; a frame drains them, and they count toward the bound.

resume.name: resume_with_nothing_queued
resume.about: A state with nothing queued resumes from an empty range.

resume.name: first_queued_after_count
resume.about: The first queued input lies past the input count.

resume.name: range_out_of_sequence
resume.about: The range does not start at the first queued input.

resume.name: range_too_long
resume.about: The range runs to the input count and past it.

resume.name: range_too_short
resume.about: The range stops before the input count.

resume.name: range_blocks_decrease
resume.about: A later input of the range lies at an earlier block.

resume.name: first_queued_is_a_batch
resume.about: The first queued input is a batch.

resume.name: first_queued_is_a_dropped_direct
resume.about: The first queued input is a direct over the payload cap.

resume.name: queued_direct_at_the_clock
resume.about: A queued direct lies at the clock, so it should have executed.

resume.name: fridge_len_mismatch
resume.about: The range admits more directs than the state queues.
